newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia government gets sequester next week - Chubais.
newsitem.headline: Russia government gets sequester next week - Chubais.

text.p: The Russian government will receive recommendations for cutting, or sequestering, spending at the end of next week, Finance Minister Anatoly Chubais told reporters on Friday.

"Work on the sequester is practically completed and it will be submitted to the government next Friday," he said. First Deputy Finance Minister Vladimir Petrov is in charge of the sequester plan and the budget as a whole, he added.
But he said the sequester meant realism rather than increased hardship for Russians.

"Budget recipients will get not less but more in the third and fourth quarters than they got in the first half of the year. This sequester is about the truth...that the government will honestly say what it can do and do it," he said.

Chubais, who is also one of two first deputy prime ministers appointed to push through new economic reforms, has said the 1997 budget is not realistic and that spending cuts must be made while $5 billion in new revenue is found.
He said budgetary problems were not hindering the country, which he said had convincingly beaten inflation and showed indications of growth.
"The budget crisis is not a crisis for the country as a whole. It is not even a crisis for the whole economy," he said.
